taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Tridens muticus normalized to current accepted Tridentopsis mutica.
look_here_first: SLIM TRIDENTOPSIS (slim tridens): find the distinctly NARROW, almost spike-like upright head with erect appressed short branches. The existing Rachel and Joey Santore photographs illustrate purple or green contracted spikelets. Next confirm usually 5–11 florets in 8–13 mm mature spikelets, and the hairs on three lemma veins; purple color or an awnless tip alone is not decisive.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local source; Kew accepts Tridentopsis mutica and lists Tridens muticus as synonym.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; exact target-zone county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Poaceae: use growth habit, ligule, panicle architecture, spikelet form, lemma hairs and awns. For this old Tridens complex, panicle openness/color and current genus placement are especially useful.
best_field_traits: Perennial grass of dry rocky/sandy grassland with often knotty, shortly rhizomatous bases and strongly contracted panicles (FNA: ~7–20[25] cm long and 0.3–0.8 cm wide). Unlike buckleyana's open branches, its spikelets are usually arranged close to the erect panicle axis; each spikelet typically has 5–11 florets. Basal midvein hairs and lateral vein hairs running beyond midpoint are specialist confirmation, not visible in current photos.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against T. buckleyana, strongly contracted, erect close branches favor mutica over an open ovate head. Counts of 6–11 fertile florets favor mutica, 3–4 favor buckleyana, but five is shared; 8–10 mm spikelet lengths overlap. Avoid treating purple-pink spikelets, a 0.5–1 mm ciliate ligule or short rhizomes as single-character proof.
crew_field_check: FIRST: original Rachel and Joey photographs show narrow, nearly spike-like flowering units; name them as visible architecture, not verified microscopic diagnosis.
Compare complete panicle width and branch placement with an open buckleyana (FNA mutica width about 0.3–0.8 cm).
Count 3 ripe spikelets: about 5–11 florets and 8–13 mm lengths in FNA; verify with millimeter ruler.
View a detached mature lemma at 10–20×: three nerves, midvein hairs on lower third/half and lateral veins hairy farther upward. Do not arrow hairs on our existing phone pictures.
At collar, find a roughly 0.5–1 mm ciliate membrane; check often narrow rolled blades and hairy lower sheaths.
Avoid creating additional cards from historical 'Tridens muticus'; keep currently unreviewed county native status provisional.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole flowering head, base and rooted crown, complete panicle with centimeter ruler
Several appressed erect panicle branches and attached spikelets at same angle as buckleyana
Three 8–13 mm intact ripe spikelets beside millimeter ruler, each floret numbered
Detached dorsal three-nerved lemma at 10–20×, mark midvein versus lateral-vein hairs
Real ciliate ligule at 1-mm scale and hairy lower sheath macro

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: Slim, almost spike-like upright 7–20(25) cm panicle only ~0.3–0.8 cm wide, with short erect/appressed branches. Confirm five to eleven fertile florets and actual lemma-nerve hairs before a species-level decision.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form_collar: Tufted perennial with knotty, shortly rhizomatous base; culms about 20–80 cm. Narrow 1–4 mm blades often rolled. Ligule a ciliate membrane about 0.5–1 mm; lower sheaths often hairy; verify at attached collar.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.spikelet_glumes: Mature spikelets approximately 8–13 mm, usually 5–11 florets. Lower glume 3–8(10) mm and 1–3-veined; upper glume 4–10 mm and 1–7-veined (Flora of North America); glumes remain after florets shed.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.lemma_palea_awn: Fertile lemma approximately 3.5–7 mm; three dorsal nerves with midvein hairs on lower third to half and lateral-vein hairs extending above midpoint. Palea about 1–2 mm shorter than lemma; lemmas effectively awnless or rarely minutely excurrent, not long-awned.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: T. buckleyana has broadly open ovate panicle, more widely separated branches and commonly 3–5 florets; five florets and 8–10 mm spikelets overlap. Tridens texanus and Eragrostis can have multi-flowered spikelets; inspect lemma nerve hairs, glume proportions and growth base.
precise_photo_arrow_gaps: Rooted perennial crown with knotty/short rhizome base and entire narrow panicle beside centimeter ruler.
Three ripe 8–13 mm spikelets at 10–20× with florets counted and lower/upper glumes individually measured.
Dissected dorsal lemma under 20×: midvein hair extent versus lateral vein hair extent, with 1-mm bar; do not annotate unresolved hairs.
Attached true 0.5–1 mm ciliate ligule, hairy lower sheath and same-angle matched T. buckleyana whole head.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — SLIM, CONTRACTED HEAD
field_id_short_tiles.short: Narrow upright panicle 7–20(25) cm long but only 0.3–0.8 cm wide.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Look for short erect/appressed panicle branches with many attached, often purple-tinged multiflowered spikelets. The Rachel and Joey Santore photos (panels 1–3) show this architecture, not a proven measured spikelet or lemma. Published measurements are from Flora of North America under the synonym Tridens muticus; don't use pink color alone.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL TARGET FLOWERING PHOTOS — COMPLETE PANICLE WITH CM SCALE NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · PERENNIAL BASE, COLLAR AND TRUE LIGULE
field_id_short_tiles.short: Knotty, shortly rhizomatous perennial base; 0.5–1 mm membranous, ciliate ligule.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Culms approximately 20–80 cm; blades 1–4 mm wide, often rolled or loosely folded. Lower sheaths often hairy. At the SAME flowering plant's blade–sheath junction, separate the tiny true ligule from sheath and collar hairs and photograph with a 1-mm bar. A close head photo does not establish crown, ligule, or stolon status; literature differs on stolons.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED VEGETATIVE CHARACTERS — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO SAME-PLANT BASE/COLLAR

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · MEASURE SPIKELETS AND BOTH GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Ripe spikelets 8–13 mm, typically 5–11 florets; glumes persist after florets drop.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Count fertile florets in at least three mature spikelets. Flora of North America: lower glume 3–8(10) mm, 1–3-veined; upper glume 4–10 mm, 1–7-veined. Broad glume ranges can reflect infraspecific variation; don't declare variety or species from a single glume measurement. Panel 3 shows real attached spikelets but lacks a calibrated glume dissection.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL ATTACHED SPIKELETS — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO MEASURED DISSECTION

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · LEMMA HAIRS, PALEA AND AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile lemma 3.5–7 mm; three veins; effectively awnless or minutely pointed.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Under 20× examine the dorsal lemma: midvein hairs on basal one-third to one-half, lateral-vein hairs often extending above midlength. Palea about 1–2 mm shorter than lemma. These tiny hair distributions are published diagnostic traits, NOT proven by the existing phone photographs; do not place submillimeter arrows without resolvable pixels.
field_id_short_tiles.status: PUBLISHED MICRO-ANATOMY — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO DORSAL LEMMA WITH 1-MM BAR

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · BUCKLEY LOOK-ALIKE: COUNT, THEN DISSECT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Slim: contracted narrow head and usually 5–11 florets; Buckley: open ovate head and usually 3–5.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panel 4 is Tridentopsis buckleyana, a different species. Counts of five florets and spikelets 8–10 mm long overlap both taxa; color and short ciliate ligules also overlap. If a full flowering head and mature dissected spikelets cannot be connected to one plant, retain a provisional Tridentopsis identification instead of asserting a confirmed species.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL OTHER-SPECIES COMPARISON — OVERLAPPING COUNTS NEED VERIFIED ANATOMY

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / TWO HANDOFFS
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: three archived target JPEGs, no calibrated reproductive dissection.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO (Grass Photo-Finish): same rooted Texas plant with knotty perennial base, entire narrow 7–20(25) cm head and centimeter ruler; 0.5–1 mm true ligule and hairy lower sheath at 1-mm scale; three mature 8–13 mm spikelets with separately measured lower/upper glumes and counted florets; detached dorsal three-veined lemma at 20× showing midvein versus lateral-vein hairs; matched Buckley head.
